The incidence of resistance varies with the organism and the geographical location; it is more frequent in or- ganisms that are also erythromycin-resistant, and some strains of meticillin-resistant Staph. aureus are also re- sistant to clindamycin. In some countries and institu- tions there is evidence of an increase in resistance amongst the B. fragilis group to about 25% of strains or more. Resistance to clindamycin by anaerobes has also been reported in 10 to 20% of Clostridium spp. other than C. perfringens, 8% of peptostreptococci, 9% of Fusobacterium spp., and 11% of Prevotella strains.
